sentence: Every inspector signed at least one certificate; the certificates need not have been the same.
setupText: Choose the passive wording that explicitly allows different certificates for different inspectors while retaining coverage of every inspector.
taskText: Every inspector signed at least one certificate; the certificates need not have been the same.
text: Choose the passive wording that explicitly allows different certificates for different inspectors while retaining coverage of every inspector. Every inspector signed at least one certificate; the certificates need not have been the same.
options: At least one certificate was signed by every inspector.
Every certificate was signed by at least one inspector.
For each inspector, at least one certificate was signed by that inspector.
There was a certificate bearing the signature of every inspector.
answer: For each inspector, at least one certificate was signed by that inspector.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2381:Quantifier dependency preserved when promoting an object
explanation: For each inspector gives every inspector a certificate-signing requirement while allowing the certificate to vary with the inspector.

rationales.At least one certificate was signed by e: This can place one certificate within the scope of all the inspectors and does not explicitly preserve the allowed inspector-by-inspector variation.
rationales.For each inspector, at least one certifi: For each inspector gives every inspector a certificate-signing requirement while allowing the certificate to vary with the inspector.
rationales.Every certificate was signed by at least: This requires coverage of every certificate, not coverage of every inspector, and leaves some inspectors potentially without a signature.
rationales.There was a certificate bearing the sign: There was a certificate selects a single certificate bearing all the signatures, which is stronger than the source.

sentence: An anonymous caller alleges that the assistant said the deposit box had been sealed. Neither claim has been checked.
setupText: Choose the sentence keeping both levels of attribution without independently confirming either sealing or the assistant's statement.
taskText: An anonymous caller alleges that the assistant said the deposit box had been sealed. Neither claim has been checked.
text: Choose the sentence keeping both levels of attribution without independently confirming either sealing or the assistant's statement. An anonymous caller alleges that the assistant said the deposit box had been sealed. Neither claim has been checked.
options: The deposit box is said by the assistant to have been sealed, as the caller has established.
The assistant is alleged by the caller to have said that the deposit box had been sealed.
The assistant is alleged to have sealed the deposit box before making a statement.
The deposit box had been sealed, as the assistant is alleged by the caller to have said.
answer: The assistant is alleged by the caller to have said that the deposit box had been sealed.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2382:Nested attribution without projecting an embedded passive event as fact
explanation: The caller remains the source of the allegation about what the assistant said, and sealing stays inside that attributed statement.

rationales.The deposit box is said by the assistant: As the caller has established upgrades the unverified allegation about the statement into established evidence.
rationales.The assistant is alleged to have sealed: This moves the allegation from the assistant's speech to the assistant's physical act of sealing.
rationales.The assistant is alleged by the caller t: The caller remains the source of the allegation about what the assistant said, and sealing stays inside that attributed statement.
rationales.The deposit box had been sealed, as the: The opening independent clause asserts sealing as fact; the final attribution does not withdraw that assertion.

sentence: The candidate was unanimously expected to be elected, but the ballot was secret.
setupText: Choose the reading that limits unanimity to the layer actually modified.
taskText: The candidate was unanimously expected to be elected, but the ballot was secret.
text: Choose the reading that limits unanimity to the layer actually modified. The candidate was unanimously expected to be elected, but the ballot was secret.
options: The sentence reports an expectation of a unanimous election result.
The sentence confirms election while leaving the voters' agreement unknown.
The unanimity concerns the prediction, not the ballot or its result.
The sentence reports unanimous support for electing the candidate rather than a prediction.
answer: The unanimity concerns the prediction, not the ballot or its result.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2383:Adverb scope across reporting passive and embedded passive infinitive
explanation: Unanimously belongs to the reporting layer: the expectation is shared, while the election result remains unasserted.

rationales.The sentence reports an expectation of a: Unanimously modifies expected, not elected; agreement among predictors does not establish a unanimous ballot.
rationales.The sentence confirms election while lea: Expected to be elected does not independently confirm that election occurred.
rationales.The sentence reports unanimous support f: An expectation about a result need not be approval of that result; people can agree on an unwelcome prediction.
rationales.The unanimity concerns the prediction, n: Unanimously belongs to the reporting layer: the expectation is shared, while the election result remains unasserted.

sentence: The deputy was persuaded by the chair to have the sealed files released to the archivist.
setupText: Choose the interpretation preserving who was persuaded and what that person was to arrange.
taskText: The deputy was persuaded by the chair to have the sealed files released to the archivist.
text: Choose the interpretation preserving who was persuaded and what that person was to arrange. The deputy was persuaded by the chair to have the sealed files released to the archivist.
options: The chair persuaded the deputy to arrange release; the physical handler is unnamed.
The chair persuaded the deputy to release the files personally; the archivist was to arrange their release.
The chair arranged release after being persuaded by the deputy; the physical handler remains unnamed.
The archivist was persuaded to release the files, with the deputy arranging the chair's involvement.
answer: The chair persuaded the deputy to arrange release; the physical handler is unnamed.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2384:Controller and agent roles in passive persuasion plus causative have
explanation: The deputy receives persuasion and is the understood subject of causative have; the participle released leaves the physical handler unexpressed.

rationales.The chair persuaded the deputy to arrang: The deputy receives persuasion and is the understood subject of causative have; the participle released leaves the physical handler unexpressed.
rationales.The chair persuaded the deputy to releas: Causative have does not require the deputy to do the physical releasing, and to the archivist marks a recipient rather than an arranger.
rationales.The chair arranged release after being p: By the chair identifies the persuader, not the person receiving persuasion; the deputy controls have.
rationales.The archivist was persuaded to release t: The archivist is the destination recipient of the files, not the subject of was persuaded or the controller of have.

sentence: The analyst reasons from the valid access token: 'The transfer ___ before it could use this token.'
setupText: Choose the wording expressing the analyst's strong inference about prior authorization, not a procedural requirement or an independently verified fact.
taskText: The analyst reasons from the valid access token: 'The transfer ___ before it could use this token.'
text: Choose the wording expressing the analyst's strong inference about prior authorization, not a procedural requirement or an independently verified fact. The analyst reasons from the valid access token: 'The transfer ___ before it could use this token.'
options: must have been authorized
had to be authorized under the procedure
was confirmed to have been authorized
was to have been authorized
answer: must have been authorized
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2385:Inferential perfect passive versus procedural and scheduled necessity
explanation: Must have been authorized expresses a strong inference about an earlier passive event, supported here by the token evidence.

rationales.had to be authorized under the procedure: Had to be authorized under the procedure states a procedural necessity, not the analyst's present inference from the token.
rationales.must have been authorized: Must have been authorized expresses a strong inference about an earlier passive event, supported here by the token evidence.
rationales.was confirmed to have been authorized: Was confirmed reports verification, which is stronger than the stated reasoning from indirect evidence.
rationales.was to have been authorized: Was to have been authorized describes a prior arrangement or expectation and does not itself express the analyst's deduction.

sentence: The survey confirms damage to the mosaic. It does not establish whether drilling caused that damage.
setupText: Choose the sentence preserving established damage but an unresolved claim about its cause.
taskText: The survey confirms damage to the mosaic. It does not establish whether drilling caused that damage.
text: Choose the sentence preserving established damage but an unresolved claim about its cause. The survey confirms damage to the mosaic. It does not establish whether drilling caused that damage.
options: The mosaic was confirmed to have been damaged, but not proved to have been damaged by drilling.
The mosaic was proved not to have been damaged by drilling.
The mosaic was not proved to have been damaged, although drilling was established as the cause.
The mosaic was confirmed to have been damaged by a cause other than drilling.
answer: The mosaic was confirmed to have been damaged, but not proved to have been damaged by drilling.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2386:Negation and causal scope under two passive evidential predicates
explanation: The first clause confirms damage; the second withholds proof only of the more specific drilling-caused damage claim.

rationales.The mosaic was proved not to have been d: Proved not to have been damaged by drilling establishes a negative causal conclusion that the survey leaves unresolved.
rationales.The mosaic was not proved to have been d: This withholds confirmation of damage itself while affirming its cause, reversing the two evidential commitments.
rationales.The mosaic was confirmed to have been da: The first clause confirms damage; the second withholds proof only of the more specific drilling-caused damage claim.
A cause other than drilling excludes drilling, whereas the survey has not resolved whether drilling was responsible.

sentence: A: 'The curator is easy to deceive.' B: 'The curator is eager to be deceived.'
setupText: Choose the analysis of the curator's role in these two grammatical sentences.
taskText: A: 'The curator is easy to deceive.' B: 'The curator is eager to be deceived.'
text: Choose the analysis of the curator's role in these two grammatical sentences. A: 'The curator is easy to deceive.' B: 'The curator is eager to be deceived.'
options: The curator receives deception in A but performs it in B because eager expresses intention.
The curator is the potential object of deception in both; only B attributes eagerness to the curator.
Both infinitives are grammatically passive, and both attribute a wish for deception to the curator.
A describes the curator's skill at deception; B describes other people's willingness to deceive the curator.
answer: The curator is the potential object of deception in both; only B attributes eagerness to the curator.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2387:Patient interpretation in an active tough infinitive versus a controlled passive infinitive
explanation: A links the curator to the missing object of active deceive; B makes the curator the subject of a passive infinitive and attributes eagerness.

rationales.The curator receives deception in A but: Eagerness does not make the curator the deceiver in B: to be deceived is passive.
rationales.Both infinitives are grammatically passi: To deceive in A is active in form with an understood object linked to the curator; easy expresses ease, not a wish.
rationales.A describes the curator's skill at decep: A evaluates how easily someone could deceive the curator, while B attributes eagerness to the curator, not to other people.
rationales.The curator is the potential object of d: A links the curator to the missing object of active deceive; B makes the curator the subject of a passive infinitive and attributes eagerness.

sentence: The volunteer got excluded from the planning group despite trying to remain involved.
setupText: Choose the inference warranted by the ordinary get-passive, without treating a possible implication as part of its meaning.
taskText: The volunteer got excluded from the planning group despite trying to remain involved.
text: Choose the inference warranted by the ordinary get-passive, without treating a possible implication as part of its meaning. The volunteer got excluded from the planning group despite trying to remain involved.

The get-passive makes the exclusion accidental, regardless of the planners' intentions.
Exclusion affected the volunteer; the sentence does not assign responsibility for causing it to the volunteer.
answer: Exclusion affected the volunteer; the sentence does not assign responsibility for causing it to the volunteer.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2388:Defeasible involvement implications in the get-passive
explanation: Got excluded presents the volunteer as affected by the event; it does not entail self-causation or willingness.

rationales.Exclusion affected the volunteer; the se: Got excluded presents the volunteer as affected by the event; it does not entail self-causation or willingness.
rationales.Using got makes the volunteer's attempt: An unwanted outcome is compatible with the get-passive, so despite introduces a coherent contrast.
rationales.The get-passive says the volunteer broug: The construction can occur where the subject bears responsibility, but it does not encode that responsibility as a requirement.
rationales.The get-passive makes the exclusion acci: Got does not determine whether the excluding group acted deliberately or accidentally.

sentence: The understudy was deliberately made to appear to have been overlooked when the casting list was circulated.
setupText: Choose the interpretation that locates the deliberate act and preserves the difference between an appearance and an established omission.
taskText: The understudy was deliberately made to appear to have been overlooked when the casting list was circulated.
text: Choose the interpretation that locates the deliberate act and preserves the difference between an appearance and an established omission. The understudy was deliberately made to appear to have been overlooked when the casting list was circulated.
options: The creation of an appearance was intentional; an actual omission is not established.
The understudy deliberately arranged to be overlooked; the circulation merely exposed the omission.
The understudy was genuinely overlooked, but the people circulating the list did not intend that omission.
The omission was accidental, although the understudy deliberately made it appear intentional.
answer: The creation of an appearance was intentional; an actual omission is not established.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2389:Intentional causation of an appearance versus the apparent passive event
explanation: Deliberately modifies made to appear; the alleged overlooking remains within appear and is not independently asserted as fact.

rationales.The understudy deliberately arranged to: The understudy is the affected subject of made to appear, not an identified arranger of the appearance or of the supposed omission.
rationales.The creation of an appearance was intent: Deliberately modifies made to appear; the alleged overlooking remains within appear and is not independently asserted as fact.
rationales.The understudy was genuinely overlooked,: An actual omission is not established by made to appear to have been overlooked, and the circulating people are not identified as the makers of that appearance.
rationales.The omission was accidental, although th: This moves intention to the understudy and treats an accidental omission as established; neither follows from the passive layering.

sentence: The locksmith attempted to open the vault, but the account gives no outcome.
setupText: Choose the edit that retains an attempted action without asserting that the vault was opened or that the attempt occurred inside it.
taskText: The locksmith attempted to open the vault, but the account gives no outcome.
text: Choose the edit that retains an attempted action without asserting that the vault was opened or that the attempt occurred inside it. The locksmith attempted to open the vault, but the account gives no outcome.
options: The vault was opened following an attempt by the locksmith.
The locksmith's attempt to open the vault was unsuccessful.
An attempt was made by the locksmith to open the vault.
The attempt to open the vault was made possible by the locksmith.
answer: An attempt was made by the locksmith to open the vault.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2390:Nonfactive attempt preserved through passive restructuring
explanation: The passive subject is an attempt, so the sentence asserts the effort while leaving the embedded opening unconfirmed.

rationales.The vault was opened following an attemp: Was opened asserts the intended result as an actual event, which the source does not confirm.
rationales.The locksmith's attempt to open the vaul: Unsuccessful asserts failure, whereas the source leaves the outcome open.
rationales.An attempt was made by the locksmith to: The passive subject is an attempt, so the sentence asserts the effort while leaving the embedded opening unconfirmed.
rationales.The attempt to open the vault was made p: Making an attempt possible identifies an enabler, not necessarily the person who made the attempt.

sentence: Only parcels that had been weighed were dispatched from the depot.
setupText: Choose the conclusion supported by the restriction, without turning a necessary condition into a guarantee.
taskText: Only parcels that had been weighed were dispatched from the depot.
text: Choose the conclusion supported by the restriction, without turning a necessary condition into a guarantee. Only parcels that had been weighed were dispatched from the depot.
options: Every parcel weighed at the depot was subsequently dispatched.
Dispatch entails prior weighing, but the converse does not follow.
A parcel's having been weighed guaranteed its dispatch from the depot.
The depot dispatched a parcel if and only if it had been weighed.
answer: Dispatch entails prior weighing, but the converse does not follow.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2391:One-way implication in a restricted passive subject
explanation: The restrictive relative clause defines the eligible group; the sentence does not assert dispatch of every member of that group.

rationales.Every parcel weighed at the depot was su: Only restricts dispatched parcels to the weighed group; it does not say that the whole weighed group was dispatched.
rationales.A parcel's having been weighed guarantee: The sentence makes weighing necessary for dispatch, not sufficient to guarantee it.
rationales.The depot dispatched a parcel if and onl: If and only if asserts both directions, whereas the source gives only dispatch implying prior weighing.
rationales.Dispatch entails prior weighing, but the: The restrictive relative clause defines the eligible group; the sentence does not assert dispatch of every member of that group.

sentence: Applicants need a sponsor to be admitted. Even sponsored applicants may be refused.

text: Choose the policy wording retaining sponsorship as necessary but not sufficient for admission. Applicants need a sponsor to be admitted. Even sponsored applicants may be refused.

explanation: Conditional on preserves the prerequisite, and the second clause explicitly withholds a guarantee of admission.

rationales.Admission is conditional on sponsorship,: Conditional on preserves the prerequisite, and the second clause explicitly withholds a guarantee of admission.
rationales.Sponsored applicants are to be admitted,: Are to be admitted gives sponsored applicants an admission entitlement that the source withholds; may be refused also weakens the rule for others.
rationales.Applicants may be admitted without spons: This creates an exception permitting unsponsored applicants to enter, which the source does not provide.
rationales.Admission is guaranteed unless an applic: This makes absence of a refused sponsorship sufficient for guaranteed admission, rather than requiring sponsorship and a separate admission decision.

sentence: The violin may or may not have been stolen. A rumor says it was stolen from the rehearsal room.
setupText: Choose the wording that keeps theft inside the rumor rather than presenting theft as independently established.
taskText: The violin may or may not have been stolen. A rumor says it was stolen from the rehearsal room.

options: The stolen violin is rumored to have been taken from the rehearsal room.
The violin, which was stolen, is rumored to have come from the rehearsal room.
The theft of the violin is rumored to have occurred in the rehearsal room.
The violin is rumored to have been stolen from the rehearsal room.
answer: The violin is rumored to have been stolen from the rehearsal room.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2393:Information projected outside a passive reporting frame
explanation: Both theft and its source location remain within the content of is rumored, leaving the event unverified.

rationales.The stolen violin is rumored to have bee: Calling it the stolen violin treats theft as part of the identifying description, outside the rumor about where it was taken from.
rationales.The violin is rumored to have been stole: Both theft and its source location remain within the content of is rumored, leaving the event unverified.
rationales.The violin, which was stolen, is rumored: The supplementary clause which was stolen asserts theft separately from the rumor about origin.
rationales.The theft of the violin is rumored to ha: The theft of the violin treats theft as given and places only its location under the rumor.

sentence: The publisher waived the translation requirement; authors remained free to supply translations.
setupText: Choose the statement that removes an obligation to translate without prohibiting translation or asserting that no translation occurred.
taskText: The publisher waived the translation requirement; authors remained free to supply translations.
text: Choose the statement that removes an obligation to translate without prohibiting translation or asserting that no translation occurred. The publisher waived the translation requirement; authors remained free to supply translations.

The articles were not required to be translated.

The articles were to be left untranslated under the waiver.
answer: The articles were not required to be translated.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2394:Negation scope over requirement versus embedded passive action
explanation: Not required places negation over the requirement, leaving both voluntary translation and non-translation possible.

rationales.The articles were required not to be tra: Required not to imposes a negative obligation: it prohibits translation rather than making it optional.
rationales.The articles were not translated because: This asserts non-translation as an actual outcome, which a waiver alone does not establish.
rationales.The articles were not required to be tra: Not required places negation over the requirement, leaving both voluntary translation and non-translation possible.
rationales.The articles were to be left untranslate: Were to be left untranslated prescribes an untranslated outcome instead of permitting authors to choose.

sentence: A: 'The sailor was allegedly wrongly detained.' B: 'The sailor was wrongly alleged to have been detained.'

explanation: The placement of wrongly changes its target from the embedded detention to the act or content of alleging detention.

rationales.Both say detention occurred and independ: In A the claim of wrongful detention is attributed; in B wrong qualifies the allegation rather than establishing an actual wrongful detention.

rationales.Both withhold judgment about whether the: B explicitly evaluates the allegation as wrong, so it does not withhold that judgment.

sentence: The conservator believes that these two paintings are forgeries.

explanation: These two paintings remains the identified subject, while their being forgeries stays within the conservator's belief.

sentence: A: 'The hatch won't open.' B: 'The hatch won't be opened.' No further context is supplied.
setupText: Choose the comparison that avoids inventing intention in an inanimate subject or certainty about an unnamed agent.
taskText: A: 'The hatch won't open.' B: 'The hatch won't be opened.' No further context is supplied.
text: Choose the comparison that avoids inventing intention in an inanimate subject or certainty about an unnamed agent. A: 'The hatch won't open.' B: 'The hatch won't be opened.' No further context is supplied.
options: A and B both attribute refusal to the hatch itself.

answer: A can describe a resistant hatch; B leaves the agent and reason unexpressed.
focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2397:Dispositional active versus agentless passive under will negation
explanation: The active intransitive construction can describe failure to open, while the passive concerns an opening event without specifying who would perform it or why it will not occur.

rationales.A and B both attribute refusal to the ha: An inanimate hatch need not have an intention in either construction; won't can express disposition or prediction.
rationales.A can describe a resistant hatch; B leav: The active intransitive construction can describe failure to open, while the passive concerns an opening event without specifying who would perform it or why it will not occur.

sentence: The absence of a reply must not be treated as evidence that permission has been granted.

explanation: Negation applies to the permitted inference from silence, not to the truth of the embedded permission claim.

rationales.It is not to be assumed from silence tha: Negation applies to the permitted inference from silence, not to the truth of the embedded permission claim.
rationales.Permission is not granted unless a reply: This creates a substantive condition for permission itself rather than a limit on what silence can be taken to show.

sentence: The board approved the recommendations on condition that they would be tested before implementation.

sentence: 'I didn't have my portrait retouched; the photographer did it without asking me.'
setupText: Choose the interpretation consistent with the speaker's denial of commissioning, followed by confirmation that retouching nevertheless happened.

The first clause says retouching was incomplete when the photographer intervened.

focusKey: coverage-passive-voice-c2-2400:Negation of causative commissioning without negation of the resulting event
explanation: In this context, not scopes over causative have: the speaker did not commission the work, although the photographer performed it.

rationales.The speaker denies arranging the retouch: In this context, not scopes over causative have: the speaker did not commission the work, although the photographer performed it.
rationales.The first clause denies any retouching,: The second clause selects the denial-of-commissioning reading of the first; the wording need not deny the resulting event.
rationales.The first clause says retouching was inc: Neither didn't have nor retouched provides a progressive or incomplete-stage claim.
rationales.The speaker accepts responsibility for a: The speaker denies the arrangement itself, not merely the identity of the person who physically retouched the portrait.
